text: In the reaction of oxalate with permanganate in acidic medium, the number of electrons involved in producing one molecule of $CO_{2}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The balanced reaction of oxalate with permanganate in acidic medium is :

$5~\text{C}_{2}\text{O}_{4}^{2-}+2\text{MnO}_{4}^{-}+16\text{H}^{+}\to 10\text{CO}_{2}+2\text{Mn}^{2+}+8\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$

In this redox reaction, the oxalate ion $\text{C}_{2}\text{O}_{4}^{2-}$ is oxidized to carbon dioxide $\text{CO}_{2}$, and the permanganate ion $\text{MnO}_{4}^{-}$ is reduced to manganese(II) ion $\text{Mn}^{2+}$.

The oxidation half-reaction, representing the change for the oxalate ion, is :

$\text{C}_{2}\text{O}_{4}^{2-}\to 2\text{CO}_{2}+2e^{-}$

From this half-reaction, it's clear that each oxalate ion produces two $CO_{2}$ molecules and releases two electrons in the process.

So, the number of electrons involved in producing one molecule of $CO_{2}$ is :

$\frac{2e^{-}}{2\text{CO}_{2}}=1e^{-}/\text{CO}_{2}$

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C: One electron is involved in the production of one molecule of $CO_{2}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Evening Slot

text: The difference in the number of unpaired electrons of a metal ion in its high spin and low-spin octahedral complexes is two. The metal ion is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The unpaired electrons in the high-spin and low-spin octahedral arrangements of each ion are compared.

$\mathrm{Mn}{}^{2+}$ ($d^{5}$): high spin $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$ has 5 and low spin $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{0}$ has 1, a difference of 4.

$\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ ($d^{6}$): high spin $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$ has 4 and low spin $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$ has 0, a difference of 4.

$\mathrm{Co}{}^{2+}$ ($d^{7}$): high spin $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{2}$ has 3 and low spin $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{1}$ has 1, a difference of 2.

$\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ ($d^{8}$): in any octahedral field the configuration is $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{2}$ with 2 unpaired electrons, so there is no separate low-spin octahedral state; diamagnetic $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ complexes are square planar, not octahedral.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Evening Slot

text:
In the cell 

$Pt(s)|H_{2}(g,  1$ bar)$|HCl(aq)|$AgCl(s)|Ag(s)|Pt(s) 

the cell potential is 0.92 V when $a 10^{–6}$ molal HCl solution is used. The standard electrode potential of (AgCl$/Ag/Cl^{–})$ electrode is : 

$\{~~$Given,  $\frac{2.303RT}{F}=0.06V$  at  $298\}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The electrode reactions are:

Anode: $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{H}{}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})+2\mathrm{e}{}^{-}$

Cathode: $2~\mathrm{AgCl}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{e}{}^{-}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})$

Overall ($n=2$): $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+2\mathrm{AgCl}(\mathrm{s})\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{H}{}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})+2\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})$

Since $E_{\mathrm{H}{}^{+}/\mathrm{H}{}_{2}}^{\circ }=0$, $E_{\text{cell}}^{\circ }=E_{\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}/\mathrm{AgCl}/\mathrm{Ag}}^{\circ }$.

In $10^{-6}$ molal HCl, $[\mathrm{H}{}^{+}]=[\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}]=10^{-6}$ and $p_{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}}=1$ bar. By the Nernst equation,

$E_{\text{cell}}=E_{\text{cell}}^{\circ }-\dfrac{0.06}{2}\log \dfrac{[\mathrm{H}{}^{+}]^{2}[\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}]^{2}}{p_{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}}}$

$0.92=E^{\circ }-0.03\log \left (10^{-24}\right )=E^{\circ }-0.03\times (-24)=E^{\circ }+0.72$

$E_{\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}/\mathrm{AgCl}/\mathrm{Ag}}^{\circ }=0.92-0.72=0.20\text{V}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Evening Slot

text: An ideal gas undergoes isothermal compression from $5m^{3}$ to $1 m^{3}$  against a constant external pressure of $4 Nm^{–2}$. Heat released in this process is used to increase the temperature of 1 mole of Al. If molar heat capacity of Al is 24 J mol$^{–1} K^{–1}$, the temperature of Al increases by :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Work done on isothermal irreversible for ideal gas 

= $-P_{$ext$}  (V_{2}$ $-$ $V_{1})$

=  $-4 N/m^{2} (1 m^{3}$ $-$ $5m^{3})$

= 16 Nm

Isothermal process for ideal gas

$\Delta$U = 0

q = $-$ w

= $-$ 16 Nm

= $-$ 16 J

Heat used to increase temperature of Al

 $q = n C_{m}_{}$ $\Delta$T

16 J = 1 $\times$ 24 $\frac{J}{mol.K}$ $\times$ $\Delta$T

$\Delta$T = $\frac{2}{3}$K

text: $5.1 g NH_{4}SH$ is introduced in 3.0 L evacuated flask at 327ºC. 30% of the solid $NH_{4}SH$ decomposed to $NH_{3}$ and $H_{2}S$ as gases . The Kp of the reaction at $327^{o}C$ is (R = 0.082 L atm mol$^{–1} K^{–1}$, Molar mass of S = 32 g mol$^{–1}$ molar mass of N = 14 g mol$^{–1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{SH}(\mathrm{s})\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{S}(\mathrm{g})$

Molar mass of $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{SH}$ $=14+5+32=51\text{g mol}^{-1}$, so $n=\dfrac{5.1}{51}=0.1\text{mol}$.

With 30% decomposed, $n_{\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}}=n_{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{S}}=0.1\times 0.3=0.03\text{mol}$, so the gas phase holds $0.06\text{mol}$.

At $T=327+273=600\text{K}$ and $V=3.0\text{L}$:

$P_{\text{total}}=\dfrac{nRT}{V}=\dfrac{0.06\times 0.082\times 600}{3.0}=0.984\text{atm}$

The two gases are formed in equal amounts, so $p_{\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}}=p_{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{S}}=0.492\text{atm}$.

$K_{p}=p_{\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}}\times p_{\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{S}}=(0.492)^{2}=0.242\text{atm}^{2}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Evening Slot
